cells.tense: You are here, in the middle of ending something, and still showing up to the work.
cells.ask: Let the next thing that no longer fits slip away today, then tell someone how that felt once it was gone.
cells.core:
The ending is real and you are not running from it. What you keep returning to is doing the clearing, and the hours alone are not hiding, they are where the work gets done. Outside it doesn't read as heroic. It just holds, and it holds you with it. A finished thing gets to be finished here, and the time you spend at it stays warm instead of tense.

So when the next ending shows up, let it go, and afterward tell someone what it was like to put it down. Not to be braver at endings. A structure falls safely when the person standing in it is steady enough to stay standing, and what you get back is a floor that doesn't need to be braced.
cells.sheetLine: You're clearing something real, and the practice is what's doing it.
cells.verb: Keeping at it until the thing comes naturally
cells.place: The stretch where something has to end for what is next to have room

cells.tense: You're bracing at a future you can't write in yet, and the practice keeps getting redone behind it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're holding tight, finish it where it stands, and tell someone you're done with it.
cells.core:
Done cleanly, this is someone who works and then lets the finished thing be finished, with the time alone giving rather than cutting off. Here the finishing keeps sliding: the refining runs past the point where it helps, as if stopping would put everything at risk, and the ending gets rehearsed far more than it gets done. The hard part of setting it down is that for a moment there's nothing in your hands.

So pick one thing and let it be done at the size it actually is, then mention it to one person. The cost is that pause with nothing to hold, and what's on the other side is space you can move in.

cells.tense: You're still standing where practice used to start, and you're not starting it.
cells.ask: Do one small piece of your work today just because it's yours, with no plan for it, and let one person know you did.
cells.core:
The starting doesn't come, and waiting has become the shape of the day. Done well, this is a person simply in the middle of the work, doing it badly and for its own sake, letting it settle without watching. What's here instead is a floor that keeps not arriving, so nothing gets stood on.

End the waiting today. Twenty minutes, badly, then tell someone. Not a fix for anything behind you, just the only way to find out what you can stay with. What it gives back is something you can stand on that your own hands made.

cells.tense: You're here, already in the practice, and you'd say it isn't practice at all.
cells.ask: Take one thing you can already do and do it slowly, on purpose, for ten minutes today, and notice that you chose to.
cells.core:
Worked well, this is a skill built quietly over years until it belongs to the one who built it, with the solitude giving something back instead of cutting anyone off. What's happening instead is that the ability seems to simply arrive where it's needed, and any suggestion that it got made gets waved away.

Take one thing you can do and try it slowly, on purpose, with nowhere to hide. Not to prove you worked for it, just to feel the choice. What you might notice is that the skill is already yours to keep, and that you're the one who was keeping it.

attempts.check: The claim to police hardest is any whisper of what happened in the past (rule 6): a person whose practice is fragile may never have had a bad scene, only a hollow where habit should sit, so the Too Little tense and core stay a location, not a story. A reader could fairly say discipline has never been the issue and the wobble is about time or company, which is why the ask is tiny and separately useful, and why none of the clauses lock them out. The ask I trust least across a card is the discipline ask itself, since it can sound like the problem is being offered back as the cure, so each ask rides on the partner medicine instead. The line that serves me most is the balanced one; kept because the partner in the seat genuinely gives that shape, but grounded on what is visible rather than on a private insight the reading claims to have.
